items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: I used to run errands for his wife, Miss Stella Oliver.

ctx.x: Louis, who would you say was the greatest influence on your life? Not in your youth, not musicians, I mean individuals. In your family or?

Well, my mother, she taught us the real things. She always said, you probably never get rich. She was wrong there, wasn't she? Well, she might be. Maybe, you know, maybe $10 million to save $10, you know. But I mean, what she means were have yachts and still got a zillion. We wasn't even thinking about that. She wasn't even thinking about it when she told me, say, but you'll always have health. So take a laxative every night of your life. And that's the finest things you ever told me. You didn't have much money…
When did you leave New Orleans?

items.title: Stella Oliver Interview, 1959-04-22
items.q: And when Louie was in St. Louis, he'd come home and stop with us.

ctx.x: Well, it would be better that way if he could have made it that way, rather than the manager takes half of their pay sometimes, too, you know.

That's what he said. But you can't make it all. No, that's right. No. Look, Louie and Louie wouldn't be in Louie Armstrong today. Yes, that's right. As if he didn't have the manager, somebody behind him. And sometimes even the men go ahead of him. Yes. See what treatment they get. Because they get an awful hard treatment. Musicians, some people don't want them in their house. Yes, that's right. And their meals, sometimes they don't have the meals and all of that. But as I can remember, so many things. And when…
Louie's still there, right? He's still, he's a thriss-criss.
